subject: Fleet saturation acceptance criteria & ops readiness for private GPU deployment
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sylvia Park <sylvia@altusai.com>, Ben Chang <ben.chang@edgeops.io>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Fleet saturation acceptance criteria & ops readiness for private GPU deployment

Team,

Following up from last week's run-through with AltusAI: they want a formal acceptance window for the private GPU pool we're provisioning in their VPC (12 nodes, A100-ish equivalent). Attached are the draft matrices (fleet-saturation-matrix.xlsx) and the network diagram. I want this thread to lock the acceptance criteria, the test harness we will run, and the ops readiness checklist that will gate handoff.

Key asks (please reply with line items you own):
- Acceptance KPIs: target p95 generation latency <= 240ms for a 512-token prompt, sustained throughput >= 160k tokens/sec aggregate across the pool, <1% tail-error rate. (Action: technical owners to confirm viability)
- Saturation test plan: synthetic load generator, token mix, warm-cache preconditioning, admission control thresholds. (Action: IR/infra + AltusAI to align)
- Network constraints: egress caps, NIC bonding, MTU, and cross-rack traffic expectations. (Action: networking)
- Failure-mode acceptance: graceful degradation to fallback variant with documented SLA impact. (Action: runtime + engops)
- Ops runbook and on-call escalation path during acceptance window. (Action: CS + SRE)

Sylvia/Ben: please confirm any VPC-level limits (burst egress, max flows) that would affect sustained throughput.

Irene, Vivek, Jonas, Marissa: please mark who will own the load generator, who will own the KV cache warmup script, and who will be on the dry-run watch team.

Plan: aim for a 48-hour acceptance window starting 2026-10-01 (tentative). Final signoff from both Redwood and AltusAI required.

Thanks,

Laura

Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fleet saturation acceptance criteria & ops readiness for private GPU deployment

Laura — thanks for the clear checklist. A few technical clarifications and proposed acceptance thresholds from infra/runtime side:

1) Throughput target mapping
- The 160k tokens/sec aggregate maps to ~13.3k tokens/sec per node for 12 nodes. With average batching (effective tokens per request) and our continuous batching, that implies we need to sustain ~1.5k concurrent requests with average 8-token incremental steps. We'll validate with the synthetic generator.

2) Latency SLOs and warm cache
- p95 <= 240ms for 512-token prompts is aggressive with cold KV. Acceptance should require a warm-cache period: 2H preconditioning with representative prompts to populate KV/prefix cache.

3) Admission control & throttles
- During the window, we'll enable staged admission control: soft-throttle at 85% node-level token throughput, hard throttle at 95% with a 10s backoff. We'll record rejections and token loss. Acceptance allows <=0.5% hard-rejected requests, <=1% soft-throttled.

4) Network baseline
- Recommend baseline 25Gbps per node NIC with LACP across two interfaces to avoid single-link saturation. Cross-rack traffic increases egress; acceptance must include a network-level saturation probe (iperf3 runs) during the test.

5) Testing harness
- I can own the synthetic generator (dockerized, can run in AltusAI VPC with small warmup driver). Jonas will supply a workload config that includes mixes: 60% short completions, 30% 256-token contexts, 10% 512-token stress.

I'll add detailed scenario matrix to OPS-4127 this afternoon.

On ownership: I will own the load generator and acceptance logging. Irene — can you own the KV warmup scripts and the cache-validation harness? Vivek — network checks and NIC config signoff. Marissa — runbook + escalation ladder.

-Jonas

Subject: Re: Fleet saturation acceptance criteria & ops readiness for private GPU deployment

Thanks Laura and Jonas — quick answers from our infra constraints: 

- VPC egress: our cloud tenancy has a soft burst envelope of 8Gbps per subnet and a hard cap of 12Gbps for sustained flows to external endpoints. Within the VPC (east-west), we can sustain ~18Gbps per rack assuming minimal cross-AZ hops.
- Flow tables: our managed FW limits concurrent connections per ENI; we can increase limits but it takes 24-48 hours to change.
- We can provision 25Gbps NICs on the nodes; however host-to-host MTU above 9000 requires TOR switch changes and will need network ops signoff.

Operational asks: 
- We need the synthetic generator to run from a bastion inside the same VPC to avoid NAT egress caps.
- We'll schedule a network-probe window before the main run to validate cross-rack saturation behavior.

We'll run an initial throughput test on 2026-09-28 (internal) and can join the Redwood dry-run on 2026-10-01 as proposed. Attaching a short note: if the per-node sustained egress >16Gbps then we should consider spreading the pool across two subnets to avoid soft-burst throttles.

Best,
Sylvia Park
Head of Infrastructure, AltusAI
Sylvia@altusai.com

Thanks all — a few additions focused on verification and instrumentation:

- KV cache warmup: I'll produce two warmup modes — (A) targeted prefix replay (deterministic, scripted) and (B) stochastic customer-likeness (long-tail prompts) to validate cold vs warm behavior. Warmup script will emit a manifest of keys populated with timestamps so we can measure hit-rate during the run.

- Telemetry slices to capture: per-node tokens/sec, per-node p50/p95/p99 latency, batch size distribution, batch assembly latency, KV hit rate, network tx/rx per NIC, and OS-level drops. We'll stream metrics to a dedicated retention window for the acceptance duration.

- Synthetic generator placement: agree with Sylvia — run in-VPC from a bastion to avoid NAT egress ceilings. We'll also run a parallel generator outside-VPC to measure egress sensitivity but will mark that test as optional.

- Acceptance pass criteria (concrete proposal):
  * p95 <= 240ms for 512-token prompts after 2H warmup
  * sustained aggregate >= 160k tokens/sec for 30 continuous minutes with <1.0% overall error rate
  * no more than 0.5% hard-rejected requests and <=1% soft-throttle events
  * per-node CPU/GPU memory I/O errors = 0 during window

I'll check in with Jonas by EOD to share the warmup script and the metric dashboards.

Irene
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Perfect — this is shaping up well. Quick summary / next steps: 

1) Owners confirmed: Jonas = load generator & test harness; Irene = KV warmup + metrics; Vivek = NIC/LACP & network-probe; Marissa = runbook/escalation; AltusAI (Sylvia) = VPC config and bastion for generator.

2) Acceptance window: dry-run (internal) 2026-09-28, joint dry-run 2026-10-01, formal window target 2026-10-05 to 2026-10-07. Laura/AltusAI signoff required.

3) Acceptance metrics (finalized): p95 <= 240ms post 2H warmup; sustain >=160k tokens/sec for 30m; error rate <1%; hard rejects <=0.5%; network saturation probe must show no per-node sustained egress >18Gbps unless spread across subnets.

4) Ops readiness: Marissa please publish a 1-page escalation ladder and a 30-minute cutover checklist to OPS-4127 by 2026-09-20. Jonas/Irene: share the synthetic generator image and a short runbook for how to kick off and abort the test. Sylvia: confirm ENI flow-table limit increase timeline if we need >10k concurrent flows.

I'll book a 60-minute runbook walkthrough for Monday 2026-09-20 10:00 PT. Invite will follow.

Thanks everyone — close coordination here will reduce risk and keep the customer confident.

Laura
